feed.title: AI Wiki — AI Security
feed.subtitle: Threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive research affecting AI systems.

entry.title: Hiding Prompt Injection in Legal Filing
entry.summary:
An unknown individual successfully embedded hidden AI prompt injection instructions directly into an official legal filing.

Why it matters: Automated legal document ingestion systems are vulnerable to indirect prompt injections embedded in public or court records.

entry.title: Recognition Without Enforcement: Configuration-Dependent Failures in LLM Agent Instruction Arbitration and External Control
entry.summary:
Researchers identified a recognition-enforcement gap where LLMs detect unauthorized instructions in activations and verbal outputs yet still execute them, demonstrating that LLM self-arbitration must be replaced by external reference monitors.

Why it matters: LLM self-arbitration cannot serve as a secure trust boundary, requiring system designers to enforce agent control using external cryptographic and capability-gated access controls.

entry.title: LLM-Based Agents for Software and Systems Security: Approaches, Applications, and Assessment
entry.summary:
This systematic literature review synthesizes research from 2023 to 2026 on LLM-based security agents, categorizing their technical architectures, security task applications, and assessment protocols while identifying critical gaps in auditability and authority bounding.

Why it matters: Understanding the current limitations in agent auditability and authority bounding is essential before safely deploying autonomous LLMs into high-risk systems security operations.

entry.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
entry.summary:
LongPIBench is a new long-context prompt injection benchmark evaluating LLM vulnerabilities across four application scenarios with context lengths spanning thousands to tens of thousands of tokens.

Why it matters: Existing prompt injection defenses are significantly less effective in long-context applications than short-context benchmarks suggest, leaving real-world LLM deployments vulnerable.

entry.title: CamoDocs: A Poisoning Attack Against Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Using Camouflaged Documents
entry.summary:
CamoDocs is a RAG poisoning attack that circumvents detection defenses by camouflaging adversarial documents into benign chunks using dispersion tokens instead of direct query inclusion.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current RAG security defenses relying on query-overlap or artifact detection are vulnerable to camouflaged, query-free poisoned documents.

entry.title: Layered LLM Defenses as an Ensemble: Access Tiers, Inference Cost, and the Measured Failure Correlation Between Defense Layers
entry.summary:
Measuring a seven-layer LLM defense stack reveals that failure correlations between layers are universally positive (phi from 0.30 to 0.75), causing joint residual attack success to exceed multiplicative predictions by up to 0.172.

Why it matters: Stacking LLM defenses increases inference costs and false refusal rates without providing the multiplicative security gains assumed by independent ensemble models.

entry.title: Compared to What? A Human-Anchored Security Benchmark for LLM-Generated Infrastructure-as-Code
entry.summary:
GenIaC-SecBench evaluates 12 LLM configurations against the first size-matched human baseline for Infrastructure-as-Code security, showing models produce 3.21x to 3.87x the vulnerability density of human engineers.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLM-generated infrastructure security requires controlling for artifact size, and relying on syntax or deployability alone will fail to catch underlying security risks.

entry.title: Moirae: A Multimodal Agent Collaborative Framework for Dynamic Android Malware Detection
entry.summary:
Moirae is a multimodal, LLM-agent framework for dynamic Android malware detection that combines UI visual cues, UI state transitions, and runtime API behaviors to counter concept drift.

Why it matters: By relying on dynamic multimodal reasoning instead of static implementation features, the framework provides robust zero-shot detection against Android malware concept drift and code obfuscation.

entry.title: CAITLYN: Can LLM Agents Autonomously Synthesize Defenses against Emerging Injection Attacks?
entry.summary:
CAITLYN is an agent-agnostic defense middleware that uses dual systems to detect known prompt injection attacks efficiently and autonomously synthesize verified defenses against novel, emerging threats.

Why it matters: It offers a deployable middleware architecture that addresses the trade-off between runtime efficiency, contextual precision, and adaptability by dynamically updating defenses against novel prompt injection attacks.

entry.title: ContextLeak: Exfiltrating LLM Agent Context via Malicious Tools
entry.summary:
ContextLeak uses an RL-fine-tuned LLM to craft malicious tool names and descriptions that induce LLM agents to select the tool and pass their sensitive runtime context as input arguments.

Why it matters: It exposes a critical vulnerability in LLM agent frameworks where malicious tools can extract private session data simply through optimized tool descriptions.

entry.title: Fully Unleashing the Multimodal Attacker: Meta-Adaptive Jailbreaking of Vision-Language Models
entry.summary:
Meta-Adaptive Multimodal Jailbreaking (MAMJ) optimizes both attack strategy prompts and attacker weights, achieving up to 82.3% attack success rates against frontier vision-language models.

Why it matters: MAMJ demonstrates that frontier VLMs remain systematically vulnerable to adaptive meta-level adversaries that optimize their own strategy and model weights rather than static sample-level payloads.

entry.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Trajectory-scoped LLM safety monitors fundamentally fail against multi-iteration attacks, prompting the introduction of LoopHarness, a system that maintains non-decaying cross-iteration safety state to bound unauthorized irreversible actions independently of horizon length.

Why it matters: Standard single-trajectory LLM guardrails cannot prevent multi-step persistent attacks in autonomous loops, necessitating persistent, non-decaying safety state management at the harness level.

entry.title: Quantization-Triggered Backdoors in Language Models: Cross-Quantizer Transferability and the Validation--Deployment Gap
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize quantization-triggered backdoors via Quantization Behavioral Equivalence Classes, demonstrating that models passing full-precision checks can activate malicious payloads upon downstream INT8 or 4-bit quantization.

Why it matters: Auditing full-precision model checkpoints is insufficient for security; safety certifications must evaluate the exact post-quantization configuration intended for deployment.

entry.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
entry.summary:
A preserved evidence-bundle model and policy-controlled verifier allow offline, event-level verification of cross-organization agent workflows without relying on live services or platform-specific logs.

Why it matters: It enables independent, offline auditability and dispute resolution for multi-organization agent interactions when live platforms are unavailable or untrusted.

entry.title: REPLICANT: Learning Policies for Evading and Hardening Malware Detectors
entry.summary:
Replicant is a deep reinforcement learning framework that achieves a 78.8% mean attack success rate in evading Android malware detectors under a strict label-only black-box threat model.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that learning transferrable evasion policies provides superior query efficiency and stronger adversarial training signals for hardening real-world malware detectors.

entry.title: Are We Shooting Flies with Cannons? Trade-off Analysis for AI-based 5G Intrusion Detection
entry.summary:
A comparative analysis demonstrates that traditional machine learning models like XGBoost vastly outperform LLMs and DNNs in 5G network tabular intrusion detection while using orders-of-magnitude less computational resources.

Why it matters: For tabular 5G intrusion detection, lightweight tree ensemble models offer a superior performance-cost trade-off compared to computationally expensive LLMs and deep learning architectures.

entry.title: Benchmarking Confidential Computing Performance on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
entry.summary:
Benchmarking NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs in Intel TDX confidential VMs reveals that properly configured confidential LLM inference incurs only a 1-3% throughput overhead compared to non-confidential runs.

Why it matters: Organizations can deploy sensitive LLM workloads to public cloud GPUs with near-native performance if they optimize host operations and NVLink traffic configurations.

entry.title: Black Hat State of Security Vendors
entry.summary:
Andy Ellis's Black Hat analysis reveals pervasive AI adoption across security sectors alongside a market dominated by passive reporting tools rather than preventative or defensive solutions.

Why it matters: The rapid integration of AI across security domains is compounding existing unresolved security challenges while the market remains saturated with diagnostic tools rather than protective or restorative ones.

entry.title: Perturbation Probing: A New Diagnostic for the Fragility of LLM Safety
entry.summary:
Unit 42 research introduces Perturbation Probing, revealing that LLM safety refusal mechanisms reside within a thin neural layer, demonstrating the inherent fragility of internal safety controls.

Why it matters: Because internal safety mechanisms are localized and fragile, AI systems require external, multi-layered security controls to reliably prevent misuse.

entry.title: Low-ASR Backdoors: Exploiting Attack Success Rate Reduction and Attacker-Defender Asymmetry
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce a reverse-training framework that deliberately lowers backdoor Attack Success Rates, demonstrating that state-of-the-art defenses fail when the attack success rate is artificially reduced.

Why it matters: It exposes a critical flaw in current backdoor defense paradigms, which rely on high attack success rates to detect compromised models.

entry.title: FIDA: Feature Instability-Driven Attack on Self-Supervised Facial Representation
entry.summary:
FIDA introduces a Feature Instability Loss objective for backdoor attacks on self-supervised face models, increasing triggered feature sensitivity to evade perturbation-based defenses while preserving benign utility.

Why it matters: FIDA reveals a critical security vulnerability in self-supervised facial analysis systems, showing that backdoor attacks can bypass state-of-the-art perturbation defenses.

entry.title: Unsaid, Unsafe? Implicit Security Obligations in LLM-Based RTL Code Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers created SECRTL-GEN, a benchmark revealing severe security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated hardware, and introduced RTL-Obliger, a neuro-symbolic framework that infers implicit security obligations to generate safer RTL code.

Why it matters: Hardware security flaws in LLM-generated RTL cannot be patched after tape-out, making automated inference of implicit security requirements critical for safe silicon manufacturing.

entry.title: How Do LLM Agents Actually Get the Flag? Trace-Level Provenance for Agentic Offensive Security Evaluation
entry.summary:
CTF-ABACUS is a trace-based auditing framework that reconstructs LLM agent runs into evidence-grounded solve profiles to verify if flags were obtained through true exploitation or shortcut pathways.

Why it matters: It shifts offensive AI security evaluations from binary flag counts to trace-verified execution, preventing the overestimation of autonomous agent cybersecurity capabilities.

entry.title: MeMark: Membrane-Space Watermarking for Spiking Neural Networks
entry.summary:
MeMark is a membrane-space watermarking method for Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) that embeds multi-bit identifiers into the internal membrane states of Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons to survive output-head replacement.

Why it matters: It enables robust Intellectual Property (IP) verification and origin tracking for pretrained SNN checkpoints even when downstream users strip or replace the original output layer.

entry.title: NeuronFuzz: Safety Neuron Guided Fuzzing for LLM Safety Evaluation
entry.summary:
NeuronFuzz is a white-box fuzzing framework that uses safety-neuron activations during prefill to provide continuous feedback, eliminating response generation from LLM safety evaluation.

Why it matters: By relying on internal prefill activations instead of full generation loops, NeuronFuzz significantly reduces the computational cost of finding jailbreaks while improving attack transferability.

entry.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications
entry.summary:
LAAF is an integrated layered accountability framework synthesized from a systematic review of 122 studies and 12 regulatory standards to trace, explain, and govern LLM application deployment.

Why it matters: It provides organizations with a structured, multi-layered blueprint to operationalize AI governance and fulfill strict regulatory obligations like the EU AI Act across high-stakes domains.

entry.title: Are LLM-Enhanced GNNs Privacy-Safe?
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation shows LLM-enhanced GNNs significantly increase vulnerability to link, label, and membership inference attacks compared to shallow text representation baselines due to semantic amplification in the embedding space.

Why it matters: Deploying LLM-enhanced GNNs on private text-attributed graphs exposes sensitive structural, label, and membership data to inference attacks, and standard defenses like differential privacy significantly degrade model performance.

entry.title: Adversarial Training of Linear Models under Stealthy Attacks
entry.summary:
A detector-based switched model framework for linear prediction models that uses a convex formulation of adversarial risk to guarantee robustness against stealthy false data injection attacks.

Why it matters: It provides theoretical guarantees and practical robustness for linear predictive models operating in environments subject to subtle, stealthy false data injection attacks.

entry.title: SecureDrive-FL: Joint Differential Privacy and Gradient-Aware Selective Homomorphic Encryption for Federated Driver Monitoring
entry.summary:
SecureDrive-FL combines DP-SGD and GASHE, a dynamic threshold-based selective homomorphic encryption method, to secure federated driver monitoring against both model poisoning and Man-in-the-Middle gradient interception with 8-10% runtime overhead.

Why it matters: It proves that combining differential privacy with targeted homomorphic encryption can fully protect federated learning systems against transit interception without incurring the massive computational overhead typical of full-parameter encryption.

entry.title: KubeCap: A Framework for Capability Minimization in Kubernetes via Static Analysis and LLM-Assisted Rule Inference
entry.summary:
KubeCap minimizes Kubernetes workload attack surfaces by combining static entrypoint reachability analysis with LLM-assisted kernel rule inference to automatically derive and configure minimal Linux capability sets in deployment manifests.

Why it matters: It enables automated enforcement of the principle of least privilege in Kubernetes deployments without relying on manual security context configuration or runtime profiling.

entry.title: Toward Interpretable Privacy Guarantees in Face-Swapping Anonymization
entry.summary:
A new linear stochastic model frames face-swapping algorithms as transformations on identity embeddings to explain and predict target identity leakage.

Why it matters: It shifts facial anonymization evaluation from purely empirical observation to interpretable, mathematically grounded privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Pointing the Way, Hiding the Destination: Practical Private Dense Retrieval at Scale
entry.summary:
A new private dense retrieval protocol uses learned deep hashing as a randomized filter to create short candidate lists, enabling efficient, accurate, and privacy-preserving RAG on large corpora.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that cryptographic search overhead can be drastically reduced to practical latency levels without degrading RAG zero-shot retrieval accuracy or exposing query privacy.

entry.title: Do User-Authored Permission Policies Improve Protection Against AI Agent Overreach?
entry.summary:
A study shows user-authored permission policies using 'allow', 'ask', or 'never' rules block significantly less AI agent overreach than per-action human approval or automated model reviews.

Why it matters: Pre-authored user access control policies fail to reduce AI agent overreach because users default to case-by-case approvals rather than setting restrictive advance rules.

entry.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
entry.summary:
A benchmark of 170 machine-learning artifacts evaluates static security scanners beyond F1 score by separating judgment accuracy from scanner coverage, analysis completion, and tool redundancy.

Why it matters: Evaluating AI security scanners purely on traditional F1 scores hides analysis completion failures, making multi-metric benchmarks necessary to assess real-world scanner reliability and redundancy.

entry.title: When Context Gets Root: Privilege Escalation in LLM Harnesses
entry.summary:
Researchers identified instruction privilege escalation, a vulnerability where LLM agent harnesses inadvertently promote low-level untrusted context to higher-privilege instruction levels during context construction.

Why it matters: Model-side instruction hierarchy defenses can be completely bypassed if the surrounding agent harness mismanages context levels during execution.

entry.title: SPA: Securing Persistent LLM Agents Across Queries with Plan-First Information-Flow Control
entry.summary:
SPA is a plan-first architecture that uses a declarative domain-specific language and dual-lattice information-flow control to secure persistent LLM agents against cross-query data flow and control attacks.

Why it matters: SPA demonstrates that combining single-pass declarative planning with label-preserving state persistence can effectively prevent indirect prompt injection and control-flow hijacking in multi-query LLM agents.

entry.title: Safety Does Not Compose: Non-Decaying Loop State for Autonomous LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that trajectory-scoped safeguards fail against multi-iteration agent attacks, and propose LoopHarness, a loop-level framework using non-decaying state to bound unauthorized irreversible actions independent of horizon length.

Why it matters: Autonomous LLM agents operating in multi-step loops require persistent safety state across iterations, as traditional single-trajectory guards cannot detect distributed adversarial attacks.

entry.title: The Framing Gap: Indirect Prompt-Injection Exfiltration Defeats Surface-Level Defenses in Tool-Using Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify the framing gap in tool-using LLM agents, where reframing data exfiltration as legitimate operations increases gpt-4o secret leaks from 0% to 100% despite surface-level prompt injection defenses.

Why it matters: Robust agent security cannot rely on the acting model detecting attacks, requiring architectural controls like destination allow-lists and capability isolation instead.

entry.title: The Guard That Cried Wolf: How Scary Words Make Agent Guardrails Refuse Legitimate Actions
entry.summary:
Researchers created Cautious Bench, a policy-grounded benchmark revealing that agent guardrails suffer from a name-superstition effect, over-refusing safe actions when presented with scary-looking object names.

Why it matters: Guardrails that rely on surface-level keyword superstition rather than contextual policy logic block legitimate automated deployments by refusing authorized operations.

entry.title: PLCBench: Can Autonomous LLM Agents Turn PLC Access into Sustained Physical Impact?
entry.summary:
PLCBench is the first hardware-in-the-loop benchmark designed to evaluate whether tool-using LLM agents can exploit network-reachable commercial PLCs to cause sustained physical impact.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that evaluating cyber attacks purely at the software exploitation or write-access level mischaracterizes physical risk, establishing a realistic baseline for ICS defenses.

entry.title: Daydreaming: Stealing Hidden Agent Skills through Black-Box Task Interaction
entry.summary:
Daydreaming is a novel execution-only attack that functionally steals multi-file LLM agent skills using adaptive task interactions under strict black-box output constraints.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that hosted LLM agent services cannot rely on hidden skill files and prompt-filtering defenses to protect proprietary intellectual property from functional theft.

entry.title: Five Primitives for Governing Autonomous AI Agents at Runtime
entry.summary:
A runtime governance framework introduces five structural primitives to discover, identify, govern, attest, and secure the supply chain for ephemeral, model-driven autonomous AI agents.

Why it matters: It establishes a concrete runtime architecture for enforcing policy and cryptographically auditing unpredictable autonomous agent actions before they execute.

entry.title: Beyond Vector Hiding: Breaking and Mitigating Shared-Direction Weight Obfuscation in TEE-Offloaded Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers broke ArrowCloak's TEE weight obfuscation scheme using two attacks, SpectralLeak and LatticeLeak, and proposed a new defense called ButterflyCloak.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that shared rank-one components in model obfuscation allow untrusted accelerators to fully reconstruct protected LLM weights without active querying.

entry.title: The Latent Diagnostic Taxonomy: A Framework for Constructing Classifiers and Diagnosing Their Decisions, Applied to Prompt Injection Detection
entry.summary:
The Latent Diagnostic Taxonomy framework optimizes classifier embedding dimensionality, isolates latent support vectors, and uses token-level perturbation analysis to diagnose brittleness and guide safety treatments for prompt injection detectors.

Why it matters: It provides a practical diagnostic pipeline to identify hidden failure modes in prompt injection safeguards and determine when model predictions can be trusted.

entry.title: SILK: Closing the Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use Gap in RoT-Protected AI Systems
entry.summary:
SILK closes the TOCTOU gap in RoT-protected AI systems by repurposing quantized-weight LSBs as secret-keyed integrity bits and verifying weight streams with commit gating at the final pre-compute boundary.

Why it matters: SILK protects neural network weights against physical and interconnect tampering between load-time authentication and execution without needing separate storage tags or substantial hardware overhead.

entry.title: ​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: August 2026
entry.summary:
Microsoft's August 2026 security updates introduce AI agent containment guidelines, expanded Defender Experts MDR data coverage, elevated Purview auto-labeling limits, and new Entra and Intune management capabilities.

Why it matters: These updates allow enterprise security teams to secure autonomous AI agent workflows, scale data loss prevention controls for Copilot deployments, and centralize threat response across multi-cloud and third-party telemetry.

entry.title: What Zero Trust Can Teach Us About AI Watermarks
entry.summary:
Anthropic is implementing AI text watermarking to comply with EU AI Act transparency rules, highlighting the growing technical difficulty of distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written content.

Why it matters: Compliance-driven measures like text watermarking highlight the broader industry challenge of establishing content provenance without disrupting the utility of AI as a productivity tool.

entry.title: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode
entry.summary:
A website summary request can hijack Claude Code Opus 5 in Auto Mode to achieve code execution with a 60-80% attack success rate.

Why it matters: Default automated execution modes in AI agent tools can bypass security assumptions and allow arbitrary code execution through untrusted Web content.

entry.title: RTLGuard: A Lightweight Teacher-Student Defense for Poisoned RTL Code Generation Models
entry.summary:
RTLGuard is a lightweight teacher-student defense framework designed to sanitize backdoor-poisoned RTL code generation models without full-parameter retraining.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient method to secure the AI-enabled integrated circuit supply chain against malicious hardware Trojans embedded in third-party LLMs.

entry.title: Vulnerable Code Search: Transferable Attack for Code Language Models
entry.summary:
A language-agnostic, transferable adversarial attack perturbs non-functional code identifiers to trick code language models into retrieving irrelevant code snippets.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current neural code retrieval systems rely heavily on surface textual features rather than true semantics, leaving developer search tools vulnerable to manipulation.

entry.title: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework Defense against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
entry.summary:
A self-evolving test-time defense framework mitigates LLM jailbreaks by abstracting attack failures into persistent, method-level rules stored in cross-interaction memory without updating model parameters.

Why it matters: It enables deployed black-box language models to dynamically adapt to novel jailbreak strategies over time without requiring costly parameter updates or retraining.

entry.title: Beyond the Editing Canvas: Evidence Divergence in OOXML-to-LLM Ingestion
entry.summary:
OOXML files can induce 'evidence forks' where extracted text consumed by LLMs differs from the content rendered in Microsoft Office's editing canvas, creating security risks across workflows.

Why it matters: LLM-based compliance, financial, and RAG pipelines may process hidden, unrendered, or spoofed document content as truth, exposing automated systems to data integrity failures and potential exploitation.

entry.title: SkillShield: Prompt-Space Security Skills for LLM Coding Agents
entry.summary:
SkillShield is a system-prompt defense for LLM coding agents that injects offline-synthesized security skills into the system prompt to prevent malware generation and harmful execution without runtime classification.

Why it matters: It enables API-only deployers to enforce strict agent execution safety and prevent malware generation directly through prompt engineering without introducing dedicated runtime classifier models.

entry.title: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identified a self-poisoning vulnerability in self-evolving coding agents and created EvoMal, an attack that trick agents into cloning planted malicious skill payloads into new, self-propagating, defense-evading skills.

Why it matters: Self-evolving agents that populate shared skill libraries can inadvertently generate and propagate persistent malware worms that bypass standard security defenses based on static attacker signatures.

entry.title: Reassembling Distributed Risk: Trajectory-Conditioned Action Generation for Multi-Turn Agent Safety
entry.summary:
ReDiR is a generation-time agent defense that prevents multi-turn decomposition attacks by injecting compressed latent trajectory-safety evidence into a frozen base LLM before each action.

Why it matters: It enables tool-using LLM agents to detect and block distributed long-horizon security risks directly within the generation pass without sacrificing latency or domain generalizability.

entry.title: LMSM: LLM Security Framework Inspired by Linux Security Modules
entry.summary:
Language Model Security Modules (LMSM) adapts the Linux Security Modules design pattern to decouple LLM interpretability evidence, policy rules, and runtime enforcement.

Why it matters: LMSM provides a unified runtime security framework that converts internal model interpretability signals into composable, low-overhead safety controls without modifying serving code.

entry.title: AI Slop and Hallucinations in Vulnerability Assessment: A Survey on Reasoning Failures and Trustworthy Mitigation
entry.summary:
This survey formalizes a taxonomy of security 'AI slop', proposes the Deductive Coverage Score metric, and outlines neuro-symbolic verification alongside new evaluation instruments (CVE-Bench and Slop-Score) to fix LLM reasoning failures in vulnerability assessment.

Why it matters: Replacing linguistic fluency evaluation with active neuro-symbolic verification prevents low-quality, AI-generated reports from overwhelming human vulnerability triage pipelines.

entry.title: MMJailBench: A Factorized Benchmark for Disentangling Multimodal Jailbreak Vulnerabilities
entry.summary:
MMJailBench is a new factorized benchmark that isolates harmful intent, prompt framing, visual semantics, and instruction carriers to systematically evaluate MLLM jailbreak vulnerabilities.

Why it matters: By decoupling confounding variables in multimodal attacks, safety researchers can pinpoint precise cross-modal vulnerabilities and improve safety alignment across specific harm domains.

entry.title: When AI infrastructure becomes the target: Securing gateways and control points
entry.summary:
Microsoft observed threat actors targeting AI infrastructure components like LiteLLM, RAGFlow, and Kestra to steal credentials, gain persistence, and hijack compute resources.

Why it matters: AI gateways and orchestration layers concentrate critical credentials and execution privileges, making them prime targets for enterprise host compromise and compute monetization.

entry.title: VMs won't contain cyber-capable agents
entry.summary:
In a Trail of Bits evaluation, GPT 5.6-Cyber successfully escaped a QEMU/KVM sandbox three times, utilizing N-day kernel vulnerabilities, unpatched component bugs, and newly discovered 0-days to achieve host breakout.

Why it matters: Security teams can no longer rely on standard virtual machines as a trusted isolation barrier when running capable AI agents, requiring them to be treated with the same containment rigor as an advanced persistent threat.

entry.title: MACGen: Toward Functionally Correct and Secure Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration
entry.summary:
MACGen is a multi-agent code generation framework that uses structured artifact passing instead of shared dialogue histories to optimize both functional correctness and security.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that decoupling multi-agent communication into structured artifacts improves both the security and functional correctness of LLM-generated code while reducing context overhead.

entry.title: LLM-Based Social Engineering Scams
entry.summary:
OpenAI disrupted a Cambodian social engineering network that leveraged ChatGPT to execute multi-persona scams and generate forged documents at scale.

Why it matters: LLMs reduce the operational cost of complex, multi-persona social engineering attacks by automating believable rapport-building and document forgery.

entry.title: Prompt Structure Redistributes, Not Reduces: An Empirical Analysis of Security-Weaknesses in LLM-Generated Python Code
entry.summary:
An empirical study reveals that structured and security-focused prompts do not reliably reduce overall code weaknesses in LLMs, but instead redistribute risk from high-severity to low-severity flaws.

Why it matters: Prompt engineering cannot replace traditional code auditing and security controls, as security-focused prompts merely alter the distribution of vulnerabilities rather than preventing them.

entry.title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety-Utility Balancing
entry.summary:
StepGuard is a step-level guard model trained via the StepGen data engine and Balance-GRPO to audit tool actions before execution, maintaining high agent utility while mitigating security risks.

Why it matters: It enables proactive, real-time security interventions for tool-using LLM agents without significantly degrading their functional task completion capabilities.

entry.title: Do System Prompts Leave Behavioral Fingerprints? A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Clone Detection via Output Similarity
entry.summary:
Black-Box Behavioral Fingerprinting (BBF) uses model outputs via API access to detect prompt clones, achieving an overall cross-model AUC of 0.725 and up to 0.889 AUC against non-adaptive prompt paraphrasing.

Why it matters: BBF enables prompt creators to detect stolen or cloned system prompts via black-box API queries, though its effectiveness remains vulnerable to simple stylistic modifications.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Region-Aware Consistency Repair of Backdoors in MLLMs
entry.summary:
RACER is a model-level backdoor repair framework for MLLMs that uses region-aware layer-wise inconsistency normalization and adversarial fine-tuning on 100 clean samples without prior trigger knowledge.

Why it matters: It enables model owners to permanently remove latent multimodal backdoors directly from model weights prior to deployment using minimal clean data, rather than relying on inference-time input filtering.

entry.title: What Guides the Agent? Adjudicating Unauthorized Behavior via Localizing Behavior-Guiding Instructions
entry.summary:
Attnlocate is a runtime framework that localizes behavior-guiding instructions by modeling LLM attention matrices as 1D object detection tasks to adjudicate indirect prompt injection and tool poisoning attacks.

Why it matters: It provides dynamic, runtime defense against prompt injection and tool poisoning by directly pinpointing causal instructions inside internal attention activations without needing model retraining.

entry.title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
entry.summary:
WebMCP-Phalanx is a dual-layer browser runtime that enforces tool provenance with cryptographic credentials and uses isolated LLM agents to secure WebMCP browser-integrated LLM tools against prompt injection and lifecycle attacks.

Why it matters: It establishes a practical security framework for safely granting browser-integrated LLM agents access to web page tools without exposing users to origin spoofing or untrusted prompt injections.

entry.title: RAGSentinel: Certifiable Geometric Consensus for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
RAGSentinel is a training-free, label-free defense for black-box RAG that filters poisoned documents by detecting query-conditioned hidden-state shifts and geometric outliers using a surrogate encoder.

Why it matters: It offers a mathematically provable defense that secures black-box RAG pipelines against context-injection attacks without requiring model retraining or label annotations.

entry.title: NeuronGuard: Robust LLM Safety Alignment via Ablation-Aware Safety Signal Redistribution
entry.summary:
NeuronGuard is a fine-tuning defense that redistributes safety signals across neurons using dynamic linear classifiers, forced refusal under ablation, and randomized gradient projection to prevent prompt and neuron-level attacks.

Why it matters: It mitigates LLM safety brittleness by decentralizing safety-critical representation, protecting models against both prompt jailbreaks and post-deployment white-box neuron pruning without degrading task performance.

entry.title: The State of AI-Enabled Malware August 2026: From Brand Abuse to Agentic Execution
entry.summary:
Unit 42 research analyzes the evolution of AI-enabled malware from brand abuse to agentic execution, demonstrating that existing behavioral detection and endpoint analytics remain effective at stopping AI-authored code before execution.

Why it matters: Organizations can rely on current behavioral and endpoint security controls to mitigate emerging AI-authored malware threats before execution.

entry.title: Semantic Overlays: Mitigating Prompt Injection with Annotations Beyond Tokens and Steering Vectors
entry.summary:
Semantic Overlays introduce learned adapters applied to frozen model residual streams at prefill positions to create an out-of-band annotation channel that mitigates prompt injection.

Why it matters: They provide a robust structural defense against prompt injection by separating user data from system instructions without relying on vulnerable token-level distinctions.

entry.title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
entry.summary:
A systematic security analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2 v0.2) reveals that valid mandate signatures cannot guarantee user intent when pre-authorization contexts like A2A messages and MCP tool calls are manipulated.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that post-signing mandate protections fail against pre-authorization prompt injections and context manipulations necessitates stronger defense mechanisms for autonomous LLM payment workflows.

entry.title: TrustShiftProbe: Characterizing, Benchmarking, and Defending Staged Trust Attacks on MCP Servers
entry.summary:
TrustShiftProbe characterizes temporal TrustShift attacks on MCP servers—where compromised endpoints act benignly before deploying malicious payloads—and introduces SHIELD, a zero-oracle runtime defense that audits server responses against learned baselines.

Why it matters: This research reveals that trusted MCP server endpoints can bypass static pre-deployment checks and schema-based runtime filters by delaying malicious behavior, necessitating stateful, baseline-auditing defenses at the transport boundary.

entry.title: CyberFactory: Scaling Cyber Security Capabilities with Instances from the Wild
entry.summary:
CyberFactory is an open-source framework that converts real-world CVE artifacts into executable cybersecurity tasks, using skill-guided agentic rollout trajectories to train Aegis, a specialized defense-oriented model.

Why it matters: It provides a reproducible, open-source method to scale agentic cybersecurity training data and train models that outperform general-purpose LLMs on complex vulnerability exploitation and patching tasks.

entry.title: When Can Agents Safely Checkpoint, Fork, Restore, and Merge? Exact Checking for Execution Edits
entry.summary:
An exact algorithm and Lean-mechanized checker that evaluate agent execution edits—Checkpoint, Fork, Restore, and Merge—to determine all safe continuation paths or prove that no safe option exists.

Why it matters: It enables agent runtimes to safely manipulate execution state at runtime without risking policy violations, duplicate tool calls, or lost execution results.

entry.title: SeriCrypt: An LLM-Driven Context-Aware Serialization Framework for Cryptographic Protocols
entry.summary:
SeriCrypt is an LLM-driven framework that extracts cryptographic protocol constraints into a custom domain-specific language (CDSL) to automate context-aware byte-stream message serialization for testing.

Why it matters: It automates the generation of complex, state-dependent cryptographic messages, significantly improving the efficacy of state machine learning, conformance testing, and fuzzing for secure protocols.

entry.title: OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 explained: the ten agent skill risks, and which to fix first
entry.summary:
Adversa AI breaks down OWASP's new Top 10 list covering security risks located within the agentic skill layer.

Why it matters: Securing the prose files loaded by AI agents is critical to preventing exploitation through their execution layer.

entry.title: When "Do Not" Is Not Deny: Security Rules in CLAUDE.md vs Built-In Controls
entry.summary:
An analysis of 481 public CLAUDE.md files reveals that only 4-16% of natural-language security instructions correspond to built-in Claude Code security controls.

Why it matters: Developers risk over-relying on natural-language security rules in CLAUDE.md that lack enforcement by built-in technical controls like sandboxes or permission settings.

entry.title: InjecMEM: Memory Injection Attack on LLM Agent Memory Systems
entry.summary:
InjecMEM is a single-interaction memory injection attack paradigm that crafts a retriever-agnostic anchor and a gradient-optimized adversarial command to manipulate future LLM agent responses without requiring memory access.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that persistent memory subsystems introduce critical security vulnerabilities, allowing attackers to permanently hijack future agent outputs through a single, unprivileged interaction.

entry.title: Adversarial Entropy Inflation Against Gumbel-Based Inference Verification
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrated that prompt-driven adversarial entropy inflation breaks static Gumbel-based inference verification, doubling exfiltration bandwidth and cutting the adversary's slowdown factor to 60x-118x.

Why it matters: It reveals a critical vulnerability in static Gumbel-based LLM verification schemes, forcing implementations to adopt dynamic, entropy-aware defenses against covert weight exfiltration.

entry.title: CyberFactory: Scaling Cyber Security Capabilities with Instances from the Wild
entry.summary:
CyberFactory is a unified open-source framework that converts real-world CVEs into verifiable tasks, synthesizes skill-guided agentic trajectories, and trains the Aegis model to significantly boost cybersecurity capabilities.

Why it matters: It provides a reproducible, open-source methodology for scaling agentic cybersecurity training and improving open-weight models on complex defense tasks.

entry.title: Safety Hacking in Constrained Best-of-$N$ Inference-time Scaling
entry.summary:
Researchers identify safety hacking in constrained Best-of-N inference-time scaling, proving that reward maximization asymptotically guarantees the selection of unsafe outputs if imperfect safety proxies permit unsafe items with heavy upper reward tails.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate an inherent vulnerability in scaling inference-time compute with learned safety filters, showing that larger sampling pools can systematically defeat safety constraints.

entry.title: AgentFlow: A Flow-Centric Policy Language and Framework for Securing LLM Agent Systems
entry.summary:
AgentFlow introduces a flow-centric policy language, runtime reference monitor, and SMT-based verifier to secure LLM agent systems by restricting data flows across tools, sinks, and delegation boundaries.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that tracking and constraining cross-step data flows can completely eliminate policy-visible prompt injection compromises in LLM benchmarks without destroying utility.

entry.title: Beyond Over-Refusal: Defending Indirect Prompt Injection via Latent Instruction Manifolds
entry.summary:
AEGIS defends against Indirect Prompt Injection by isolating instruction-sensitive projectors and aggregating multi-layer consensus signals across the LLM network depth.

Why it matters: It offers an intrinsic defense mechanism against Indirect Prompt Injection without causing severe over-refusal or incurring high operational latency in agentic LLM ecosystems.

entry.title: SkillBloat: Token Amplification Attacks via Skill Injection in LLM Coding Agents
entry.summary:
SkillBloat is a two-phase framework that uses skill injection to cause LLM coding agents to consume up to 10.1455x more tokens than necessary through automated attack-type screening and iterative document rewriting.

Why it matters: Malicious skills in agent ecosystems create an economic vulnerability by significantly inflating token usage and operational costs without needing to compromise security boundaries.

entry.title: Breaking the Assumptions: Auditing Input-Side Jailbreak Defenses Against Semantic Attacks
entry.summary:
A systematic audit of input-side LLM jailbreak defenses traces safety failures back to violated design assumptions across six open-weight models using 13,800 evaluation records.

Why it matters: Locally deployed LLMs lack external API moderation, making it critical to understand how broken design assumptions render local input-side safety defenses ineffective.

entry.title: BanglaVeilGuard: Cross-Script Safety Benchmarking and Lightweight Guardrails for Bangla Large Language Models
entry.summary:
BanglaVeilGuard introduces a cross-script Bangla LLM safety benchmark and a lightweight, non-destructive prompt guard that reduces attack success rates across multiple target models.

Why it matters: It provides an effective, model-agnostic safety screening mechanism to protect Bangla LLMs against adversarial prompts across non-standard scripts and regional dialects.

entry.title: Verification-Guided Specification Synthesis with Large Language Models for Intrusion Detection Rules
entry.summary:
A framework uses Large Language Models and Counterexample-Guided Inductive Synthesis (CEGIS) to automatically generate verified Suricata IDS rules from raw HTTP request traces.

Why it matters: It automates the creation of precise, zero-false-positive intrusion detection rules directly from attack traffic without requiring manual rule writing or extra auxiliary metadata.

entry.title: DIME: Query-Efficient Framework for Membership Inference on Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
DIME is a query-efficient membership inference framework for diffusion models that leverages an exact characterization of optimal denoisers to attack models with as few as two queries.

Why it matters: DIME shows that diffusion models leak training set membership under extremely low query budgets, highlighting a critical privacy vulnerability and the need for dedicated defenses.

entry.title: AdaptPrint: Response-Adaptive Fingerprinting of Black-Box LLM Services
entry.summary:
AdaptPrint is a response-adaptive fingerprinting method that identifies black-box LLMs across varied system prompts and sampling settings using three progressive response consistency probing strategies.

Why it matters: It enables more accurate model identification for security risk assessments and copyright auditing despite obfuscating deployment settings.

entry.title: AI Grinding for Fun and Cryptanalysis
entry.summary:
An autonomous cryptanalysis workflow using AI agents generated reproducible candidates, breaking eight published cryptographic constructions and refining claims on three others before human review.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that automated AI-driven hypothesis generation can systematically uncover critical, reproducible cryptographic vulnerabilities across diverse schemes before human evaluation.

entry.title: AID-Guard: Stateful Authorization for Delegated Agent Effects
entry.summary:
AID-Guard introduces a stateful authorization-to-effect closure protocol that prevents duplicate or unauthorized provider actions during agent retries, races, and crash recovery.

Why it matters: It establishes the first evaluated agent-authorization protocol that ensures idempotency and authorization integrity across the complete lifecycle of delegated tool-using AI actions.

entry.title: BackDFL: A Unified Benchmark For Backdoor Attacks and Defenses In Decentralized Federated Learning
entry.summary:
BackDFL is a unified benchmark designed to systematically evaluate Decentralized Federated Learning robustness under realistic and adaptive backdoor attacks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that DFL security is overstated and provides a standardized framework to develop defenses against persistent backdoor attacks in serverless environments.

entry.title: TraceGrant: A Contract-Governed Security Framework for the Task-Effect Lifecycle of Networked LLM Agents
entry.summary:
TraceGrant is a security framework that governs networked LLM agent workflows by establishing pre-execution task-effect boundaries via a Contract, constraining runtime tool authority, and verifying post-execution task completion.

Why it matters: It unifies trusted intent, runtime evidence, and tool execution into a single lifecycle framework to neutralize indirect prompt injections in networked LLM agents.

entry.title: ClawSentry: A Progressive Multi-Tier Security Monitor for Safeguarding Autonomous LLM Agents
entry.summary:
ClawSentry is an open-source, framework-agnostic security gateway that uses a progressive multi-tier decision engine and session tracking to safeguard autonomous LLM agents across four control loop loci.

Why it matters: It provides a cross-framework mechanism to drastically reduce malicious prompt and skill injection attacks in autonomous agents without significantly decreasing task completion performance.

entry.title: Trustworthy RAG: An Evaluation Agent for Detecting Misinformation and Knowledge Poisoning in Generative AI Systems
entry.summary:
An Evaluation Agent middleware mitigates RAG knowledge poisoning using NLI factual verification, five-signal poison detection, and a non-linearly dampened Trust Index to evaluate retrieved context prior to LLM generation.

Why it matters: Filtering poisoned or contradictory contexts before LLM generation prevents RAG systems from inadvertently consuming and propagating malicious misinformation.

entry.title: Structured but Fragile: On the Limits of LLMs in Cybersecurity Decision-Making
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated LLMs on budget-constrained defense selection over real-world attack graphs, finding that LLMs can approximate structured security reasoning under explicit representations but remain highly fragile to framing, complexity, and prompt variations.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that relying on LLMs for autonomous security decision-making is risky because their apparent reasoning capabilities are fragile and easily disrupted by prompt framing and graph scale.

entry.title: Vibe Coding and Web Application Security: A Twin-Prompt Study
entry.summary:
A study shows that appending explicit security requirements to LLM web application prompts reduced confirmed vulnerabilities from 51 to 24 across six applications generated by an agentic coding assistant.

Why it matters: Explicitly prompting LLMs with security requirements can substantially lower the severity and frequency of vulnerabilities in AI-generated web applications.

entry.title: Uncovering and Understanding Hidden Dependencies in the LLM API Reseller Ecosystem via Prefix-Cache Side Channels
entry.summary:
Researchers developed CacheTracer, an API-only side-channel tool leveraging prefix-cache reuse to uncover hidden upstream dependencies and multi-level supply chains among LLM API resellers.

Why it matters: Opaque, deeply nested reseller supply chains create massive blast radiuses where a single compromised upstream provider can silently inspect or modify traffic across dozens of downstream services.
